version.note: The source identifies the orchestral song, but not its performing edition or editorial alterations. The listening notes use the low-voice orchestral score, C. F. Kahnt plate 4460, for passage-level scoring; they do not claim this exact printed edition was on the performers’ desks.

performers.note: The Commons description identifies all three performing credits; the independent catalogue corroborates the pairing.

date.note: Commons and the Naxos reissue back cover give 20–21 June 1955. The two-day span is for the cycle’s sessions; the movement is not assigned to a particular day.

place.note: The Naxos back cover identifies Jesus-Christus-Kirche in Berlin for these sessions; this is session evidence, not evidence that the Commons transfer comes from that reissue.

label.note: Commons names its source as “CD audio EMI”. This is the identified CD source label, not an assertion about the original session medium.

catalogue.note: No catalogue number identifying the CD used for the Commons upload is supplied. Naxos 8.111300 documents the same recording sessions, but is a different reissue: its catalogue number and Mark Obert-Thorn restoration credit are not attributed to the unidentified EMI CD.

matrixTakeSides.note: No matrix, take or original side identification is supplied. The absence of those details is not treated as proof that no historical identifiers exist.

credits.note: The Commons uploader is not treated as a transfer or mastering engineer. No such credit for this particular CD-to-Ogg transfer is identified.

date.note: No transfer date is supplied; upload dates and historical recording dates are not substituted for it.

processing.value: Commons provides an uploaded Ogg Vorbis file and an MP3 access derivative.
processing.note: The embedded Ogg encoder is Xiph.Org libVorbis I 20100325 (Everywhere). The original session medium, earlier mastering, noise reduction and editing history are unestablished.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative supplied by Wikimedia Commons; uploaded source: Ogg Vorbis

composition.value: The Sibley Music Library marks its early printed orchestral score, including Rückert’s text, as public domain.
composition.note: The catalogue gives Mahler’s dates as 1860–1911 and Rückert’s as 1788–1866. This refers to the historical composition and text, not an unidentified modern performing edition; the catalogue’s inconsistent publication year is not adopted.

recording.value: Territorial — Commons applies PD-EU-audio to the sound recording.
recording.note: The template concerns the rights of performers and phonogram producers, not merely the composition. The recording is accepted on that EU territorial basis. United States status and worldwide clearance are not established; no US pre-1926 claim is made.

rights.creditLine: Gustav Mahler, Kindertotenlieder, III. Wenn dein Mütterlein; Dietrich Fischer-Dieskau, baritone; Berlin Philharmonic; Rudolf Kempe, conductor. Recorded 20–21 June 1955. EMI CD source via Wikimedia Commons; Commons states PD-EU-audio (EU territorial status; US status unestablished).
